analyzed_vuln.description: Stack buffer overflow due to out-of-bounds read/write on fixed-size local arrays `num_samples[WMALL_MAX_CHANNELS]` and `contains_subframe[WMALL_MAX_CHANNELS]` in `decode_tilehdr`. The loop uses `for (c = 0; c < s->num_channels; c++)` without validating that `s->num_channels <= WMALL_MAX_CHANNELS`, so crafted stream/header state with too many channels causes access past the stack arrays (ASan shows overflow at line 361 on `num_samples[c]`). Crash is observed in `decode_tilehdr` called from `decode_frame`.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: In the WMALOSSLESS decoder path (`decode_packet` -> `decode_frame` -> `decode_tilehdr`), attacker-controlled bitstream/header values must lead to `s->num_channels` exceeding `WMALL_MAX_CHANNELS` (array bound used for local tile header bookkeeping). Then `decode_tilehdr` iterates up to `s->num_channels` and accesses `num_samples[c]`/`contains_subframe[c]` out of bounds, triggering stack-buffer-overflow even with very small input.
